title: Free Trial Terms for Loop+ Membership Plans
content:
Every Loop+ Membership plan offers a free trial of a set number of calendar days. Three plan terms govern the trial: its length, the lookback period that withholds the trial from a buyer whose earlier trial or paid membership ended recently, and the point at which the first fee is charged once the trial is over.

## Trial terms by plan

| Plan | Length of the free trial (calendar days) | Trial lookback (months) | When the first fee is charged after a trial |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loop+ Access Monthly | 30 | 12 | the day after the trial end date |
| Loop+ Student Monthly | 180 | 12 | the day after the trial end date |
| Loop+ Student Annual | 180 | 12 | the day after the trial end date |
| Loop+ Monthly | 30 | 12 | the day after the trial end date |
| Loop+ Annual | 30 | 12 | the day after the trial end date |
| Loop+ Household Annual | 30 | 12 | the day after the trial end date |

## Definitions

1. **Length of the free trial** is stated in calendar days, a whole number: 180 calendar days on the two student plans and 30 calendar days on the other four plans.
2. **Trial lookback**: a buyer whose trial or paid membership ended within this many months before sign-up gets no trial. On every Loop+ Membership plan the lookback is 12 months.
3. **First charge after a trial**: on every plan the first fee is charged on the day after the trial end date.

## Points of judgement

- The trial length belongs to the plan the buyer signs up for: a buyer joining Loop+ Student Annual is looking at a 180-day trial, a buyer joining Loop+ Annual at a 30-day trial.
- The lookback is the same 12 months on every plan, so moving the sign-up to another Loop+ plan does not change the lookback period that applies.
- Hypothetical illustration: on a plan whose trial ends on 30 April, the first fee is charged on 1 May, the day after the trial end date.
